title: Canonical prompt seeding and contract validator for live tool streams
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Build a canonical prompt seeding process and an automated contract validator (validator) that runs against live-style tool/function streaming scenarios to catch API, schema, and tokenization regressions before they reach production. Background: We have recurring subtle regressions when combining streaming, tool calls, and structured output schemas: truncated JSON, message boundary drift, interleaved token loss when KV cache warmup differs, and model shim incompatibilities. This ticket defines the seed corpus, the validator rules, CI gates, and the rollout plan for baking the validator into PR pipelines and nightly regression runs.
acceptance_criteria: Validator binary (stream-contract-validator) produces deterministic pass/fail for a seeded set of 120 canonical prompts covering: simple streaming-only, interleaved-toolcalls, nested structured JSON outputs, partial-on-error toolfallbacks, and explicit token-boundary edgecases.
CI job 'stream-contract-check' is added to the runtime repo and blocks merges on regression signals above configured thresholds (see CI integration).
Regression dashboard tile created in Console for contract failures by model variant, region, and commit hash with linked failure artifacts.
False-positive rate verified: < 2% over a 7-day smoke run on the seed corpus. Any failure labeled as 'non-deterministic' must include repro instructions.
SRE/QA runbook added with steps to triage validator failures and automatic rollback policy for Dedicated deployments if a canary crosses availability thresholds.
test_plan: Assemble a canonical seed corpus of 120 prompts: 40 streaming-only, 40 toolcall-interleaved (including function schemas), 20 structured-output-only (strict JSON schema), 20 KV-cache-warmup sequences (varying prefix lengths).
Create synthetic variations using noise-injection (token-drop, latency skew, chunk-split) to simulate protocol drift; store variations in gs://redwood-test-artifacts/streaming-seed/2025-02

Implement validator checks: (1) message boundary reconciliation (sequence ids + checksum), (2) JSON schema strictness enforcement with detailed path errors, (3) toolcall ACK/complete pairing checks, (4) KV cache warmup consistency heuristics (prefix replay), (5) tokenization deltas compared to golden token stream.
Define per-check thresholds and severity: hard-fail for missing toolcall completions or invalid JSON; soft-fail (warning) for minor tokenization deltas that do not change parsed output shape.
Add model-shim compatibility tests: run seed corpus against model variants and shim layers (quantized, float16, patched attention) and record divergence fingerprints to enable targeted rollbacks.
Produce a canonical failure artifact format (ndjson) per run containing raw byte-stream, chunk timestamps, parsed events, and validator errors. Attach artifacts to CI and dashboard for debugging.
ci_integration: New GH Action job: .github/workflows/stream-contract-check.yml runs stream-contract-validator across the seed corpus on PRs that touch runtime/streaming or api/protocol files.
Job matrix: nodes = [small-local, dedicated-canary], models = [model-v1, model-v1-quant], runtime-configs = [default, kv-warmup-on].
Gating thresholds: block merge if >= 1 hard-fail OR >= 3 soft-fail warnings in a single run; for CANARY (nightly) job, alert if hard-fail count increased by > 30% week-over-week.

Nightly regression: scheduled job 'stream-contract-nightly' runs full matrix, uploads artifacts to S3 and updates the regression dashboard. Failures auto-create centralized issue with reproduced artifacts.
Integrate with Slack channel #streaming-regressions to surface failures with direct links to run artifacts and suggested first-step runbook commands.
